newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves incentives for Intel plant.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves incentives for Intel plant.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday approved a proposal to grant investment incentives to Intel Corp. if it chooses the Czech Republic to build a $300 million to $500 million computer microchip plant.
"The government approved some investment incentives in the case of Intel," said Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl after a regular government meeting. He gave no further details.

Intel representatives said Monday the Czech Republic is on a short list of countries which the U.S. semiconductor firm is evaluating to build the plant. Locations in the Middle East and Asia are also under consideration, Intel said.

Local media have reported that Intel is seeking tax holidays and other incentives, but the facility would generate up to 12 billion crowns ($350 million) in revenue for the Czech government over eight years.
The plant is expected initially to employ 3,000 people and could grow to as many as 9,000 jobs at full capacity.
Industrial areas near the Czech cities of Plzen and Pardubice are under consideration, the daily Pravo has reported.
Japan's Matsushita has just opened a $66 million Panasonic television plant in the Borska Pole industrial park near Plzen.
